description: Make make lint substantially faster and easier for delivery agents to interpret by reusing safely compiled Go checker executables, running independent targets concurrently with clear failure attribution, and hiding package-boundary findings already recognized by the merged baseline policy unless --all is requested, without weakening any lint rule or changing PR #1844 ignore semantics.

context.customerAsk: Reduce the wall time and output volume of make lint without weakening any gate: run independent lint targets concurrently, avoid repeated Go checker compilation costs, preserve target-specific failure attribution and standalone behavior, and hide the approximately 172 recorded package-boundary migration violations unless --all is requested.
context.problem: Delivery agents repeatedly prove that branches add no new lint violations relative to main, but the current lint lane runs independent gates sequentially, pays go run startup and compilation costs for each custom checker, and floods normal output with recorded package-boundary debt. This makes delivery slower and obscures the violations an agent is actually responsible for.
context.solution: Provide one cross-platform lint execution path that prepares reusable gitignored checker executables, schedules independent targets with bounded concurrency, captures and labels target results, and fails if any requested target fails. Filter package-boundary presentation through the already-merged baseline classification so default output shows only unrecorded findings while --all exposes complete diagnostics without changing classification or exit behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: make lint runs the requested independent lint targets with bounded concurrency, waits for their terminal results, and exits non-zero if any requested target fails.

Custom Go checker targets use reusable compiled executables from a gitignored cache on the normal lint path; changed checker inputs cannot silently reuse stale behavior, and the supported fallback path preserves the checker's arguments, output, and exit status.
Concurrent execution produces target-delimited output and a final result that names each failed target, while successful gates and existing LINT_TARGETS and root-variable overrides remain usable.

On an unchanged tree, package-boundary default output omits every finding already recognized by the merged recorded-baseline/ignore rules; a deliberately introduced unrecorded boundary violation is printed and makes both the standalone gate and aggregate lint lane fail.

pkgboundarycheck --all displays the complete diagnostic output, including recorded debt, but does not alter classification, ignore matching, blocking counts, or exit status; no PR #1844 ignore-rule semantic is reimplemented or changed.

The PR records same-machine, same-environment before-and-after timings for documented main and branch revisions across at least three unchanged-tree runs and their medians, with the optimized median at least 30% lower, and records the command/output from a scratch new-boundary-violation proof.
Quality gates pass: typecheck and tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file or inventory churn are resolved against current origin/main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Reuse compiled checker executables
userStories.description: As a delivery agent, I want lint checks to reuse safely prepared checker executables so repeated lint proof does not pay a separate go run compilation cost for every custom Go checker.
acceptanceCriteria: The normal lint path prepares custom Go checker executables in a gitignored cache and invokes those executables with the same arguments and environment values as their existing checker targets.

Repeating an unchanged checker target reuses valid compiled output, while changing relevant Go build inputs causes the executed checker behavior to be rebuilt rather than silently using a stale executable.
Direct invocation of an affected lint sub-target remains supported and produces the same pass/fail result and checker diagnostics as before.
An explicit supported fallback path uses go run with equivalent arguments and exit propagation; a genuine compile failure remains visible and cannot be converted into a passing check.

Focused process-level tests prove executable reuse, stale-input invalidation, argument forwarding, fallback behavior, and non-zero checker exit propagation without asserting a hard-coded command inventory.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added the cross-platform cmd/lintcheck process driver and routed every Go checker used by lint, including the nested ownership checker, through its reusable executable cache. The cache key includes the checker transitive Go build inputs, module files, compiler/build environment, and target package; compiled output is published atomically under the gitignored .cache/lint-checkers path. Direct lint sub-targets retain their arguments and inherited environment. LINT_CHECKER_FALLBACK=1 uses the original go run path with a -exec status shim so Windows preserves checker streams and exact exit codes; compiler failures remain non-zero and visible. Focused process tests cover unchanged reuse, transitive-input invalidation, argument/environment forwarding, fallback output and exit propagation, and compile failure visibility. Focused checker tests, go vet ./cmd/lintcheck, make backend-size, make pkg-file-count, make pkg-maint, and make typecheck pass. make pkg-boundary still reports the pre-existing boundary debt assigned to story thr-lint-speed-003.

userStories.title: Run independent lint targets concurrently with clear attribution
userStories.description: As a delivery agent, I want independent lint targets to run concurrently and report target-scoped outcomes so lint completes sooner without hiding which gate needs action.
acceptanceCriteria: make lint schedules requested independent targets with bounded concurrency greater than one by default, supports an explicit positive job limit, and never exceeds that limit.

The driver waits for every started target to reach a terminal state and returns non-zero when one or more targets fail; its final summary names every failed target and provides an actionable standalone rerun name.
Output from concurrent targets is delimited by target so diagnostics cannot be mistaken for another gate's output, and a successful run ends with an unambiguous success result.
LINT_TARGETS selection, checker root overrides, platform-appropriate executable handling, and non-Go gates such as UI lint, scripts, and vet retain their established observable behavior.

Deterministic tests with controllable commands prove actual overlap, job-limit enforcement, mixed success/failure aggregation, output attribution, and argument/environment forwarding; tests do not depend on wall-clock speed thresholds.
The PR reports at least three same-machine unchanged-tree runs for main and the optimized branch, includes raw and median wall times, and shows at least a 30% reduction in the optimized median.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Added cmd/lintlane as the cross-platform bounded worker-pool driver used by make lint. LINT_JOBS defaults to 4 and accepts any explicit positive limit; every started target runs to terminal completion, captures stdout/stderr independently, emits target-delimited output in requested order, and reports every failed target with a standalone make rerun. LINT_TARGETS and command-line root overrides continue through child Make invocations, non-Go targets retain their recipes, Windows child Make runs use an available native Git sh.exe when present to avoid concurrent cmd.exe temporary-batch contention, and each target gets an isolated temporary environment for platform process artifacts. Aggregate lint compiles cmd/lintcheck once per lane into a unique temporary executable under the gitignored checker cache, while direct checker targets and LINT_CHECKER_FALLBACK=1 remain supported. Deterministic tests cover actual overlap, job-limit enforcement, terminal waiting, mixed failure aggregation, target attribution, success output, argument/environment forwarding, positive job validation, and target selection. Benchmark on main revision 947152348 versus optimized commit c931a4013 used equal-work commands make -k lint and make lint LINT_JOBS=4 with the default target set: valid main runs were 173.292s, 184.979s, and 163.251s (median 173.292s, exit 2 for the existing pkg-boundary, packaged-factory-consumption-check, ownership-inventory-check, and deadcode debt); optimized runs were 150.522s, 85.924s, and 87.756s (median 87.756s, exit 2 with the same four named failures), a 49.4% median reduction. One host-terminated baseline attempt (282.178s, exit -1) was excluded from the three-run median. go test -race ./cmd/lintlane, make test, make typecheck, focused lint gates, and aggregate fallback verification pass.

userStories.title: Hide recorded package-boundary debt by default
userStories.description: As a delivery agent, I want normal package-boundary output to show only unrecorded violations so I can immediately distinguish branch regressions from accepted migration debt.
acceptanceCriteria: Default package-boundary output does not print individual findings or debt-count summaries for violations already recognized by the PR #1844 recorded-baseline/ignore policy.
A fixture containing recorded debt and one unrecorded violation prints only the unrecorded violation by default, identifies its rule and affected package/import context, and exits non-zero.
A fixture containing only recorded debt produces a quiet passing/default result consistent with the existing ignore policy and does not list the recorded findings.
--all prints the recorded and unrecorded diagnostic sets in stable, target-readable form while preserving exactly the same blocking classification and exit status as default mode.

The aggregate make lint path uses quiet mode by default, still catches a deliberately introduced new boundary violation, names pkg-boundary as failed, and supports an intentional all-diagnostics invocation.

Focused behavioral tests cover quiet clean output, mixed recorded/new findings, --all, and unchanged exit semantics using the already-merged baseline matcher rather than a second ignore implementation.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented quiet package-boundary presentation without changing scanner rules or existing exact baseline matchers. The checker compares classified finding fingerprints with a selected Git base tree (PACKAGE_BOUNDARY_BASE_REF or origin/main), hides only findings already present there by default, preserves stale baseline entries as blocking, and fails open if the base cannot be materialized. It no longer falls back to HEAD: when no trustworthy origin/main, upstream/main, or local main ref exists, every current finding remains visible and blocking; an explicitly invalid -base-ref or PACKAGE_BOUNDARY_BASE_REF returns a clear non-zero error. Exact matcher-approved findings are retained for --all, which emits recorded findings and summaries while using the same visible blocking count and exit status. Make exposes PACKAGE_BOUNDARY_ALL=1 and PACKAGE_BOUNDARY_BASE_REF for intentional diagnostics. Behavioral fixtures cover recorded-only quiet success, mixed recorded/new failure, a new finding added to an already-recorded file, exact matcher diagnostics under --all, aggregate make lint attribution, a committed violation with only HEAD available, and an invalid explicit base. Scratch proof command: go run ./cmd/pkgboundarycheck -root <scratch-root>; terminal result exited 1 and printed the committed.go prohibited domain transport diagnostic, the active generated-code exception summary, and [agent-factory:pkg-boundary] found 1 package-boundary violation(s), followed by exit status 1. Focused checker tests and vet, backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, typecheck, and the merged-tree maintenance gates pass. The broad make test command was attempted but exceeded its five-minute local limit while shared workspace unit lanes were contending; the changed package suite passes in full.
